steps.body: An **L-shaped** solid isn't a box, so no single l × w × h fits it. The trick: **cut it into boxes yourself**. Our L: a bottom slab 5 units long, 2 wide, 2 tall, with a 2 × 2 × 2 block sitting on top of its left end. Cut along the block's base, find each box's volume, add.

widget.prompt: The L's bottom slab is 2 wide and 2 tall, both locked. Slide the length out to 5 and watch what each unit of length is worth.

commonBuilds.feedback: 4 cubes is one unit of length — a single 2-by-2 slice. The slab runs 5 of those.
16 is four units of length. One more 2-by-2 slice completes the slab.

widget.successFeedback: 20 cubic units. Every unit of length brought a whole 2-by-2 cross-section of 4 cubes — which is why splitting an L-shaped solid works at all: each piece is a plain box, and no cube belongs to two pieces at once.
widget.lowFeedback: Shorter than the slab. Each step of length adds a full 2-by-2 slice — 4 cubes.
widget.highFeedback: Longer than the slab. Pull the length back toward 5.

predict.prompt: The slab is 2 wide and 2 tall. Each extra unit of LENGTH will add…
predict.reveal: 4 — a whole 2-by-2 cross-section arrives with every unit of length. This is why an L-shaped solid can be split and its parts added: each part is a plain box built the same way, and no cube is ever counted by two of them.

explanationVariants: The block is 2 × 2 × 2 = 8; the whole L is 20 + 8 = 28.
Cut at the block's base: 20 cubes below, 8 above, 28 total.

widget.prompt: The 2 × 2 × 2 block sits on the slab (volume 20). What is the whole L's volume in cubic units?

commonErrors.feedback: 20 is the slab alone. Add the block on top: 20 + 8 = 28.
40 is the 5 × 2 × 4 box the L fits inside — but the notch above the slab's right end is empty. Only 20 + 8 = 28 cubes are really there.

steps.body: Here's the satisfying part: **a different cut gives the same answer**. Slice the same L straight down at the block's edge instead. Now the pieces are a tall box 2 long, 2 wide, 4 tall, and a short box 3 long, 2 wide, 2 tall. Every cube still gets counted exactly once — so any legal split must agree.

explanationVariants: Tall piece 2 × 2 × 4 = 16, short piece 3 × 2 × 2 = 12; 16 + 12 = 28 — same as before.
Different cut, same cubes: 16 + 12 = 28, matching the 20 + 8 split.

widget.prompt: The vertical cut gives a 2 × 2 × 4 box and a 3 × 2 × 2 box. What total volume does this cut give, in cubic units?

commonErrors.feedback: 16 is the tall piece only (2 × 2 × 4). Add the short piece: 16 + 12 = 28.
12 is the short piece only (3 × 2 × 2). Add the tall piece: 16 + 12 = 28.

widget.fallbackFeedback: 16 + 12 = 28 — the same total as the horizontal cut.

widget.prompt: Marco computed the L's volume as 5 × 2 × 4 = 40. What went wrong?

options.label: He measured the box the L fits inside — the empty notch isn't part of the solid
options.feedback: Right — that bounding box includes the 12-cube notch above the slab's right end, which is empty air. The L itself is 28.

options.label: He should have added 5 + 2 + 4 instead
options.feedback: Adding edges is a different mistake — it never gives volume. Marco's real error is counting the empty notch as if it were filled.

options.label: He multiplied the edges in the wrong order
options.feedback: Order never changes a product. The problem is that 5 × 2 × 4 measures a full box, and the L has an empty notch inside that box.

hints: Is the L really a full 5 × 2 × 4 box?
What sits above the slab's right end?
explanationVariants: The bounding box counts the empty notch; the L is 28, not 40.
40 − 28 = 12 cubes of empty notch got wrongly counted.
Split at the step: twelve cubes below, six above, 18 in all.

widget.prompt: A step-shaped solid is a 4 × 3 × 1 box with a 2 × 3 × 1 box on top of one end. What is its volume in cubic units?

commonErrors.feedback: 12 is the bottom box only. Add the top step: 12 + 6 = 18.
24 is the full 4 × 3 × 2 box the step fits inside — but the space above the lower step is empty. Add the real pieces: 12 + 6 = 18.

explanationVariants: Slab 6 × 2 × 2 = 24 plus block 2 × 2 × 2 = 8 gives 32 cubic units.
Any legal cut of this L totals 32 — the bounding 6 × 2 × 4 box (48) overcounts the empty notch.

widget.prompt: An L-shaped solid is a 6 × 2 × 2 slab with a 2 × 2 × 2 block on top of one end. What is its volume?

options.label: 24 cubic units
options.feedback: 24 is the slab alone. Add the block on top: 24 + 8 = 32.

options.label: 48 cubic units
options.feedback: 48 is the full 6 × 2 × 4 box around the L — the notch above the slab is empty. The solid holds 24 + 8 = 32.

takeaways: Odd solids split into boxes: find each l × w × h, then add.
Any legal cut gives the same total — every cube counts once.
Never use the box a solid merely fits inside; empty notches aren't volume.
steps.teaser: course complete! Next course: plotting points on the coordinate plane.

concept.body: Quick rewind. **Split the solid into boxes, then add.** A small L made of a 2 × 2 × 2 box (8 cubes) and a 2 × 1 × 2 box (4 cubes) has volume 8 + 4 = 12. One box at a time, then one addition.

explanationVariants: Eight cubes in one piece, four in the other: twelve.

widget.prompt: A solid splits into a 2 × 2 × 2 box and a 2 × 1 × 2 box. What is its total volume in cubic units?

commonErrors.feedback: 8 is the first piece only (2 × 2 × 2). Add the second: 8 + 4 = 12.
4 is the second piece only (2 × 1 × 2). Add the first: 8 + 4 = 12.
